plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Just as the meadows turn tired and golden, pale lilac-pink goblets rise from the bare earth. They have no leaves, so they look like they appeared by magic. Each goblet opens wide to the autumn sun.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late August to October, with flowers appearing above ground from late August or early September
plants.location: Meadows and grasslands across Western and Central Europe, including the British Isles
plants.funFact: The leaves don't appear until the following spring. The plant is also highly toxic, and it is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: Glossy, golden-yellow cups look like crocuses and pop up from dry, sun-baked ground at the start of autumn. They are a bright sign that the rains have returned to the Mediterranean hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to October, usually triggered by the first autumn rains
plants.location: Mediterranean region, from Iberia and southern Europe to Turkey and the Middle East
plants.funFact: Many botanists think this is the 'lily of the field' mentioned in ancient texts. It survives the Mediterranean summer by staying dormant as a bulb underground.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A spectacular crimson flower head sits on a stalk, ringed by petal-like bracts. It looks like a firework frozen mid-burst, and nectar-seeking honeyeaters flock to it in the Australian spring bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, mainly September to October around Sydney (later in cooler areas)
plants.location: Sandstone bushland within about 200 km of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The 'flower' is really a dense cluster of hundreds of tiny flowers surrounded by showy bracts. It is the floral emblem of New South Wales.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a bowl of silky pink petals around a crown of fuzzy white and pink. It lights up the fynbos slopes in the late southern winter and early spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly June to October, which covers the late southern winter and early spring
plants.location: Fynbos vegetation of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to an ancient plant family that dates back to the time of Gondwana, and fynbos fires help it regenerate.
